claims.text: Introducing a ductile, rare-earth-free metallic phase can enhance the integrity of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy.
The metallic-phase intervention can preserve the alloy's caloric response.
Cu or Ag would be suitable ductile metallic phases for the intervention.
The ductile phase can be incorporated by mechanical alloying or spark plasma sintering.
The distribution of the ductile phase and its interaction with the matrix control the structural response.
The ductile phase acts as a crack-arresting medium.
Crack arrest by the ductile phase enhances toughness and structural integrity.
The intervention preserves the high-entropy-alloy matrix microstructure.
Preservation of the matrix microstructure maintains the caloric response.
The modified material will have a compressive strength greater than 200 MPa.
The modified material will show more than a 10% increase in strain to failure relative to the unchanged alloy.
The intervention will limit the reduction in entropy change to less than 10% relative to the unchanged alloy.
The predicted behavior applies at magnetic fields of 0–5 T, pressures of 0–100 MPa, and temperatures of 250–350 K under uniaxial compression.
The modified material has proposed operating limits of 400 K and 200 MPa.
The optimal ductile-phase content and distribution are unknown.
A greater than 20% decrease in caloric response would falsify the hypothesis.
A less than 10% increase in compressive strength would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires less than a 10% caloric-response reduction, but the experiment only falsifies the hypothesis above a 20% reduction, leaving a 10–20% reduction inconsistent with the prediction yet non-falsifying.
